title: Convexity of the Fourier square functional
statement: For a natural number $n$, let $c$ assign a real number $c(S)$ to each subset $S$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and suppose $c(S)\ge 0$ for every $S$. On the space of real-valued functions on $\{-1,1\}^n$, the functional that sends $f$ to $\sum_S c(S)\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform average of $f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, is convex.
